globalStyle:
COCOA & CHROME — the homeowner's chosen D design with BLUE AND BUTTER-YELLOW ACCENTS, rich ESPRESSO-BROWN WOOD and polished SILVER/CHROME. This is a correction: the previous neutral design looked too much like Mineral & Walnut. Match the actual material/color language in style reference IMAGE 3. This must be visibly distinct from an all-beige walnut room.
Deep cocoa/espresso brown wood with luxurious matched natural grain, substantial cabinetry and freestanding drawer units on CONTINUOUS RECESSED FLOOR PLINTHS, no little furniture legs, no floating consoles/nightstands. Thin honed pale taupe stone tops where useful. Polished SILVER/CHROME is a deliberate visible finish on sculptural opal lighting, hardware, taps, picture lights and occasional small tables; NO brass or gold metal. Richness through scale, materials and proportion, not ornate trim or excessive build-outs.
Warm putty/mushroom subtly mineral walls and light ivory doors/trim make WARM WHITE Cloud seating, chairs and upholstered beds feel intentional. Neutral natural OAK floors and ivory loose rugs. Preserve all four bedroom wood floors/rugs. Beautiful clear ivory drapes, daylight, green living plants where appropriate.
BLUE is a clearly visible recurring design element in LARGE BLUE-AND-WHITE ABSTRACT ART, ink/navy/cobalt cushions, throws, bedding and selected ceramics. Not just a microscopic blue mark or gray abstract. BUTTER-YELLOW is a smaller but clearly visible highlight in cushions, flowers or ceramics, enough to register at room scale without dominating. No giant yellow wall or matching furniture set. Mix colors naturally: roughly 70% quiet architectural envelope/white upholstery, 20% dark cocoa furniture, 8% blue, 2% yellow within styled areas; these are visual guidelines not measured surface percentages. Green plants complement the blue/yellow, they do not replace them. Do not desaturate blue or yellow away. Keep creamy white fabrics distinct from wall color and dark brown grain distinct from black.
Photoreal high-end interior editorial photograph, clear daylight and believable scale. No new room, new openings, new ceilings or service moves. Keep actual camera and exterior views. No people, watermark, labels or text except explicitly requested inscriptions.
